files.notes: 7 translucent floor plates (MTR..2/F) plus a translucent podium. files.title: Festival Walk vertical circulation, 3D (lifts / escalators / stairs / ramps)
files.notes: 29 genuine floor-to-floor connectors, separated from the 48 flat site surfaces using the CSDI FeatureType domain and Gradient field. Each connector's two floors are resolved by matching its ends against the published floor networks (a connector's ends land at 0.00 m from the floor it serves). Carries floor_from, floor_to, mode (link / shaft / incline) and rise_m. The app draws each connector with a different z on each vertex, so lifts are vertical shafts and escalators slope between floors.

files.title: Festival Walk flat site surfaces (podium decks, traffic islands, crossings, footways)
files.notes: 48 flat surfaces from the CSDI routes that have no floor id and are NOT vertical circulation. They are outdoor podium decks, traffic islands, crossings and footways, which belong on the terrain rather than inside the building. Kept separate so they are not drawn as a flat mesh through the mall.

files.title: Steep slope polygons - ground steeper than 30 degrees
files.notes: 33,231 polygons of ground exceeding a 30 degree gradient, 113.29 km2 = 10.09% of Hong Kong's land area (1,122.26 km2). Slope is the MAXIMUM gradient within each 20 m cell (Horn's method) from the LandsD 5 m DTM, because 22,700 recorded incidents sit in cells whose mean slope is under 30 degrees but whose max is over it. 8-connectivity, so corner-touching steep cells merge into one hillside. Area reconciliation error 0.0 m2, 0 invalid geometries. EPSG:2326 (HK1980).

files.title: Maximum slope raster (20 m)
files.notes: Maximum gradient within each 20 m cell, degrees, from the LandsD 5 m DTM (Horn's method). 3187 x 2400 at 20 m, float32, EPSG:2326 (HK1980), nodata -9999.

files.title: Steep slopes of Hong Kong - two-panel map
files.notes: Panel A: five slope classes with 40,000 of the 124,020 recorded landslide incidents overprinted. Panel B: the >30 degree polygons alone over the gentler land, with the six largest regions labelled by area. Scale bar, north arrow and source line. Text overlap and off-canvas checks both pass at zero; a pixel probe confirms all five classes are rendered.

files.title: Slope class polygons - ArcGIS Online pack
files.notes: Zipped shapefile of the 106,874 five-class slope polygons, EPSG:4326 (WGS84). AGOL returns 2,000 records per request by default - enable 'Allow >2000 features per request' on the source view or the layer draws only its first 2,000 features.

files.title: Steep slope polygons - GeoJSON with original field names

scripts.description: Fetch and validate the VIIRS night-lights nights. Rejects blank (all-zero) rasters by CONTENT, not by HTTP status, because GIBS returns 200 with an empty raster for unserved dates.
Score the 41 campsites on darkness, access, facilities and horizon. Asserts every factor is populated, no score is NaN, and that the access term yields more than 20 distinct values.

Build the two-panel figure. Checks text overlap and off-canvas text BEFORE saving, then verifies the rendered pixels over the bright city, the dark country and the dark sea each match the source raster value at that location.
Copy the outputs into the repo layout and verify each shipped file.
Extend this manifest with the camping entries and verify every entry against the file on disk.
Fetch the OSM coastline via /map, with adaptive bbox splitting on HTTP 400 and backoff on HTTP 429. The coastline is an orientation overlay only - it is NOT used as a land mask.
Merge the bbox-clipped coastline fragments into complete ways. Merging by way id instead of node sequence keeps only the last fragment of any way crossing a box boundary, which guts the coastline.
Flood-fill the land from the sea over a rasterised coastline. Kept for the record: it fails where the coastline is not closed, which is why the shipped map applies no land mask at all.
Record the build scripts in this manifest and verify each one against the file on disk.

Download the published script and its two inputs into a fresh temporary directory and run the build there with only the environment variables set. Proves the repo copy works off the author's machine, which is the thing a student actually needs.
